Main.sentence: Jakarta , [b] officially the Special Capital Region of Jakarta , [c] is the ___E:capital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_city)___ and largest city of ___E:Indonesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia)___ and an autonomous region at the provincial level.

Lying on the northwest coast of ___E:Java U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java)___ , the world's ___E:most populous island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_by_population)___ , Jakarta is the ___E:largest metropole U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_ASEAN_by_population)___ in ___E:Southeast Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia)___ and serves as the diplomatic capital of ___E:ASEAN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASEAN)___ .

The Special Region has a status equivalent to that of a ___E:province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_Indonesia)___ and is bordered by the province of ___E:West Java U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Java)___ to the south and east and ___E:Banten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banten)___ to the west. Its coastline faces the ___E:Java Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_Sea)___ to the north, and it shares a maritime border with ___E:Lampung U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lampung)___ to the west. ___E:Jakarta's metropolitan area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta_metropolitan_area)___ is ___E:ASEAN's second largest economy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ASEAN_country_subdivisions_by_GDP)___ after ___E:Singapore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore)___ .
In 2023, the city's ___E:GDP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_domestic_product)___ PPP was estimated at US$724.010 billion.
Jakarta is the economic, cultural, and political centre of Indonesia.

Although Jakarta extends over only 661.23 km 2 (255.30 sq mi) and thus has the smallest area of any ___E:Indonesian province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_Indonesia)___ , its ___E:metropolitan area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta_metropolitan_area)___ covers 7,076.31 km 2 (2,732.18 sq mi), which includes the satellite cities of ___E:Bogor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogor)___ , ___E:Depok U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depok)___ , ___E:Tangerang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangerang)___ , ___E:South Tangerang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Tangerang)___ , and ___E:Bekasi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bekasi)___ , and has an estimated population of 32.6 million as of 2022 [update] , making it the ___E:largest urban area in Indonesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_metropolitan_areas_in_Indonesia)___ and the ___E:second-largest in the world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_largest_cities)___ (after ___E:Tokyo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Tokyo_Area)___ ).

Jakarta ranks ___E:first among the Indonesian provinces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Indonesian_provinces_by_Human_Development_Index)___ in the ___E:human development index U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index)___ .

Jakarta's business and employment opportunities, along with its ability to offer a potentially higher ___E:standard of living U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_of_living)___ compared to other parts of the country, have attracted migrants from across the Indonesian ___E:archipelago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archipelago)___ , making it a melting pot of numerous cultures.
Jakarta is one of the ___E:oldest continuously inhabited cities in Southeast Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_oldest_continuously_inhabited_cities)___ .

Established in the fourth century as ___E:Sunda Kelapa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunda_Kelapa)___ , the city became an important trading port for the ___E:Sunda Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunda_Kingdom)___ .

At one time, it was the overseas administrative center of the ___E:Dutch East India Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_India_Company)___ , as well the Imperial Dutch capital of the ___E:Dutch East Indies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_Indies)___ , when it was known as ___E:Batavia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batavia,_Dutch_East_Indies)___ .

Jakarta was officially a city within ___E:West Java U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Java)___ until 1960 when its official status was changed to a ___E:province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_Indonesia)___ with ___E:special capital region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_districts_and_territories#Indonesia)___ distinction.
As a province, its government consists of five administrative cities and one ___E:administrative regency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thousand_Islands_(Indonesia))___ .

Jakarta is an ___E:alpha world city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_city#GaWC_study)___ and the ASEAN secretariat's seat. Financial institutions such as the ___E:Bank of Indonesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_Indonesia)___ , ___E:Indonesia Stock Exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia_Stock_Exchange)___ , and corporate headquarters of numerous ___E:Indonesian companies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_companies_of_Indonesia)___ and ___E:multinational corporations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation)___ are located in the city. Jakarta, as Indonesia's largest Muslim-majority city, is known for its tradition of religious tolerance and pluralism.
The Istiqlal Mosque, the largest in Southeast Asia, stands as a symbol of the city's commitment to interfaith harmony.

Jakarta's main challenges include rapid urban growth, ecological breakdown, air pollution, gridlocked traffic, congestion, and ___E:flooding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floods_in_Jakarta)___ due to subsidence and water extraction (sea level rise is relative, not absolute).

Part of North Jakarta is sinking up to 17 cm (6.7 inches) annually, meanwhile the southern part is relatively safe. This has made the northern part of the city more prone to flooding and one of the fastest-sinking capitals in the world.

In response to these challenges, in August 2019, President ___E:Joko Widodo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joko_Widodo)___ announced plans to ___E:move the capital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_of_Indonesia#Relocation_to_Nusantara)___ from Jakarta to the planned city of ___E:Nusantara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nusantara_(city))___ , in the province of ___E:East Kalimantan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Kalimantan)___ on the island of ___E:Borneo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo)___ .

The ___E:MPR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Consultative_Assembly)___ approved the move on 18 January 2022. The Indonesian government is not abandoning Jakarta after announcing plans to move the country's capital, its planning minister said, pledging to spend US$40 billion, which is more than the cost to build ___E:Nusantara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nusantara_(city))___ , to save the city in the next decade.
Jakarta has been home to multiple ___E:settlements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_settlement)___ .
Below is the list of names used during its existence:

The ___E:Buni people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buni_culture)___ is a prehistoric ___E:clay pottery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_pottery)___ culture that flourished in coastal northern ___E:West Java U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Java)___ , Jakarta, and ___E:Banten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banten)___ around 400 BC to 100 AD  [page needed] and survived until 500 AD.

___E:Sundapura U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarumanagara)___ is the name mentioned in the ___E:Tugu inscription U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugu_inscription)___ from ___E:Tarumanagara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarumanagara)___ , a kingdom in coastal West Java. The strategic geographical position of coastal West Java, which corresponds to today modern Jakarta, is a commanding region that controls the Sunda Strait.

This location is strategic in regard to ___E:Sumatra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumatra)___ and also its connection to Asian continent of ___E:India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India)___ and ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ .

After the fall of the Tarumanagara, the name of city was changed to 'Sunda Kelapa' or 'Coconut of Sunda,' growing to be the main harbour for the ___E:Sunda Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunda_Kingdom)___ due to its desirable location.

The name 'Jakarta' is derived from the word Jayakarta ( ___E:Devanagari U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devanagari)___ : जयकर्त), which is ultimately derived from the ___E:Sanskrit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit)___ जय jaya (victorious),  and कृत krta (accomplished, acquired),  thus Jayakarta translates as 'victorious deed', 'complete act', or 'complete victory'.

It was named for the Muslim troops of ___E:Fatahillah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatahillah)___ which successfully defeated and drove the Portuguese away from the city in 1527, eventually renaming it 'Jayakarta.'  ___E:Tomé Pires U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A9_Pires)___ , a Portuguese apothecary, wrote the name of the city in his ___E:magnum opus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suma_Oriental)___ as Jacatra or Jacarta during his journey to the ___E:East Indies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Indies)___ .

After the Dutch East India Company took over the area in 1619, they renamed it 'Batavia', after the ___E:Batavi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batavi_(Germanic_tribe))___ , a Germanic tribe who were seen as the ancestors of the Dutch.

The city was then also known as Koningin van het Oosten (Queen of the Orient), a name that was given for the urban beauty of ___E:downtown Batavia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kota,_Jakarta)___ 's ___E:canals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gracht)___ , mansions and ordered city layout.

After expanding to the south in the 19th century, this nickname came to be more associated with the suburbs (e.g. ___E:Menteng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menteng)___ and the area around ___E:Merdeka Square U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merdeka_Square,_Jakarta)___ ), with their wide lanes, green spaces and villas.

During the ___E:Japanese occupation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_occupation_of_the_Dutch_East_Indies)___ , the city was renamed as Jakaruta Tokubetsu-shi (ジャカルタ特別市; Jakarta Special City) .
After the Japanese surrender, the name was changed to 'Jakarta'.

The north coast area of western Java including Jakarta was the location of prehistoric ___E:Buni culture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buni_culture)___ that flourished from 400 BC to 100 AD.  The area in and around modern Jakarta was part of the 4th-century ___E:Sundanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundanese_people)___ kingdom of ___E:Tarumanagara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarumanagara)___ , one of the oldest ___E:Hindu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu)___ kingdoms in Indonesia.

The area of ___E:North Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Jakarta)___ around ___E:Tugu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampung_Tugu)___ became a populated settlement in the early 5th century.

The ___E:Tugu inscription U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugu_inscription)___ (probably written around 417 AD) discovered in Batutumbuh hamlet, Tugu village, ___E:Koja U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koja,_Jakarta)___ , ___E:North Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Jakarta)___ , mentions that King ___E:Purnawarman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purnawarman)___ of Tarumanagara undertook hydraulic projects; the irrigation and water drainage project of the Chandrabhaga river and the Gomati river near his capital.

Following the decline of ___E:Tarumanagara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarumanagara)___ , its territories, including the Jakarta area, became part of the Hindu ___E:Kingdom of Sunda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunda_Kingdom)___ .
From the 7th to the early 13th century, the port of Sunda was under the ___E:Srivijaya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Srivijaya)___ maritime empire.

According to the Chinese source, Chu-fan-chi , written circa 1225, ___E:Chou Ju-kua U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhao_Rukuo)___ reported in the early 13th century that Srivijaya still ruled Sumatra, the Malay peninsula, and western Java ( ___E:Sunda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunda_Kingdom)___ ).
The source says the port of Sunda was strategic and thriving, mentioning ___E:pepper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_pepper)___ from Sunda as among the best in quality.
The people worked in agriculture, and their houses were built on wooden piles.

The harbour area became known as ___E:Sunda Kelapa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunda_Kelapa)___ ( ___E:Sundanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundanese_language)___ : ᮞᮥᮔ᮪ᮓ ᮊᮨᮜᮕ ) and by the 14th century, it was an important trading port for the Sunda Kingdom.
The first European fleet, four Portuguese ships from ___E:Malacca U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malacca)___ , arrived in 1513 while looking for a route to obtain spices.

The Sunda Kingdom ___E:made an alliance treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luso_Sundanese_padr%C3%A3o)___ with the Portuguese by allowing them to build a port in 1522 to defend against the rising power of the ___E:Demak Sultanate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demak_Sultanate)___ from central Java.  In 1527, ___E:Fatahillah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatahillah)___ , a Pasai-born military commander of Demak attacked and conquered Sunda Kelapa, driving out the Portuguese.
Sunda Kelapa was renamed Jayakarta,  and became a fiefdom of the ___E:Banten Sultanate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banten_Sultanate)___ , which became a major Southeast Asian trading centre.

Through the relationship with Prince Jayawikarta of the Banten Sultanate, Dutch ships arrived in 1596. In 1602, an English ___E:East India Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company)___ (EIC) voyage led by Sir ___E:James Lancaster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Lancaster)___ arrived in ___E:Aceh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aceh)___ and sailed on to ___E:Banten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banten)___ , where they were allowed to build a trading post. This site became the centre of English trade in the Indonesian archipelago until 1682.  Jayawikarta is thought to have made trading connections with the English merchants, who were rivals with the Dutch, by allowing them to build houses directly across from the Dutch buildings in 1615.
When relations between Prince Jayawikarta and the Dutch deteriorated, his soldiers attacked the Dutch fortress.
His army and their EIC allies, however, were defeated by the Dutch, in part owing to the timely arrival of ___E:Jan Pieterszoon Coen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Pieterszoon_Coen)___ .
The Dutch burned the EIC trading post and forced them to retreat to their ships.
The victory consolidated Dutch power, and they renamed the city Batavia in 1619. [citation needed]
Commercial opportunities in the city attracted native and especially Chinese and Arab immigrants.
This sudden population increase created burdens on the city. Tensions grew as the colonial government tried to restrict Chinese migration through deportations.

Following a revolt, 5,000 Chinese were ___E:massacred U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1740_Batavia_massacre)___ by the Dutch and natives on 9 October 1740, and the following year, Chinese inhabitants were moved to ___E:Glodok U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glodok)___ outside the city walls.
At the beginning of the 19th century, around 400 Arabs and Moors lived in Batavia, a number that changed little during the following decades.
Among the commodities traded were fabrics, mainly imported cotton, batik and clothing worn by Arab communities.

The city began to expand further south as epidemics in 1835 and 1870 forced residents to move away from the port. The Koningsplein , now ___E:Merdeka Square U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merdeka_Square,_Jakarta)___ was completed in 1818, the housing park of ___E:Menteng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menteng)___ was started in 1913,  and ___E:Kebayoran Baru U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kebayoran_Baru)___ was the last Dutch-built residential area.  By 1930, Batavia had more than 500,000 inhabitants,  including 37,067 Europeans.
The city was expanded in 1935 through the annexation of the town of Meester Cornelis, modern ___E:Jatinegara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jatinegara)___ .

On 5 March 1942, the Japanese captured ___E:Batavia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batavia,_Dutch_East_Indies)___ from Dutch control, and the city was named Jakarta (Jakarta Special City (ジャカルタ特別市, Jakaruta tokubetsu-shi) , under the special status that was assigned to the city).

After the war, the Dutch name Batavia was internationally recognised until full Indonesian independence on 27 December 1949. The city, now renamed Jakarta, was officially proclaimed the national capital of Indonesia.

After ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ ended, Indonesian nationalists declared independence on 17 August 1945,  and the government of Jakarta City was changed into the Jakarta National Administration in the following month.

During the ___E:Indonesian National Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_National_Revolution)___ , Indonesian republicans withdrew from ___E:Allied U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II)___ -occupied Jakarta and established their capital in ___E:Yogyakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yogyakarta)___ .

After securing full independence, Jakarta again became the national capital in 1950.  With Jakarta selected to host the ___E:1962 Asian Games U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_Asian_Games)___ , ___E:Sukarno U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukarno)___ , envisaging Jakarta as a great international city, instigated large government-funded projects with openly nationalistic and ___E:modernist architecture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modernist_architecture)___ .

Projects included ___E:a cloverleaf interchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semanggi_Interchange)___ , a major boulevard ( ___E:Jalan MH Thamrin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jalan_MH_Thamrin_(Jakarta))___ -Sudirman), monuments such as ___E:The National Monument U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monas)___ , ___E:Hotel Indonesia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel_Indonesia)___ , a shopping centre, and a new building intended to be the headquarters of ___E:CONEFO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONEFO)___ .

In October 1965, Jakarta was the site of ___E:an abortive coup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30_September_Movement)___ attempt in which six top generals were killed, precipitating ___E:a violent anti-communist purge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_mass_killings_of_1965%E2%80%9366)___ which killed at least 500,000 people, including some ethnic Chinese.
The event marked ___E:the beginning of Suharto's New Order U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transition_to_the_New_Order)___ .
The first government was led by a mayor until the end of 1960 when the office was changed to that of a governor.

The last mayor of Jakarta was ___E:Soediro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soediro)___ until he was replaced by ___E:Soemarno Sosroatmodjo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soemarno_Sosroatmodjo)___ as governor.

In 1966, Jakarta was declared a 'special capital region' ( Daerah Khusus Ibukota ), with a status equivalent to that of a province separated from ___E:West Java U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Java)___ .
Based on law No. 5 of 1974 relating to regional governments, the Jakarta Special Capital Region was confirmed as the capital of Indonesia and one of the country's then 26 provinces.

Lieutenant General ___E:Ali Sadikin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Sadikin)___ served as governor from 1966 to 1977; he rehabilitated roads and bridges, encouraged the arts, and built hospitals and a large number of schools.
He cleared out slum dwellers for new development projects — some for the benefit of the Suharto family,  — and attempted to eliminate rickshaws and ban street vendors.
He began control of migration to the city to stem overcrowding and poverty.
Foreign investment contributed to a real estate boom that transformed the face of Jakarta.

The boom ended with the ___E:1997 Asian financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Asian_financial_crisis)___ , putting Jakarta at the centre of violence, protest, and political manoeuvring.

After three decades in power, support for President ___E:Suharto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suharto)___ began to wane. Tensions peaked when four students were ___E:shot dead U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trisakti_shootings)___ at ___E:Trisakti University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trisakti_University)___ by security forces. ___E:Four days of riots and violence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_1998_riots_of_Indonesia)___ in 1998 ensued that killed an estimated 1,200, and destroyed or damaged 6,000 buildings, forcing Suharto to resign.
Much of the rioting targeted ___E:Chinese Indonesians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Indonesian)___ .

In the post-Suharto era, Jakarta has remained the focal point of democratic change in Indonesia.  ___E:Jemaah Islamiyah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jemaah_Islamiyah)___ -connected bombings occurred almost annually in the city between 2000 and 2005,  with ___E:another in 2009 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Jakarta_bombings)___ .

In August 2007, Jakarta held ___E:its first-ever election to choose a governor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Jakarta_gubernatorial_election)___ as part of a nationwide decentralisation program that allows direct local elections in several areas.
Previously, governors were elected by the city's legislative body.

Between ___E:2016 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Jakarta_attacks)___ and ___E:2017 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Jakarta_bombings)___ , a series of terrorist attacks rocked Jakarta with scenes of multiple suicide bombings and gunfire. ___E:Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Bakr_al-Baghdadi)___ claimed responsibility for the attacks on behalf of ___E:Islamic State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State)___ .

During the ___E:Jokowi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jokowi)___ presidency, the Government adopted a plan to move Indonesia's capital to ___E:Nusantara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nusantara_(planned_city))___ after 17 August 2024,  but this has not occurred due to delays.
On 30 November 2024, President ___E:Prabowo Subianto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prabowo_Subianto)___ signed Law No. 151/2024, officially revoking Jakarta's status as the capital.
Jakarta covers 661.23 km 2 (255.30 sq mi), the smallest among any ___E:Indonesian provinces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_Indonesia)___ .

However, its metropolitan area covers 6,392 km 2 (2,468 sq mi), which extends into the two bordering provinces of ___E:West Java U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Java)___ and ___E:Banten U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banten)___ .

The ___E:Greater Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jabodetabek)___ area includes three bordering regencies ( ___E:Bekasi Regency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bekasi_Regency)___ , ___E:Tangerang Regency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangerang_Regency)___ and ___E:Bogor Regency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogor_Regency)___ ) and five adjacent cities ( ___E:Bogor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogor)___ , ___E:Depok U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depok)___ , ___E:Bekasi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bekasi)___ , ___E:Tangerang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangerang)___ and ___E:South Tangerang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Tangerang)___ ).

Jakarta is situated on the northwest coast of ___E:Java U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java)___ , at the mouth of the ___E:Ciliwung River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliwung_River)___ on ___E:Jakarta Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta_Bay)___ , an inlet of the ___E:Java Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_Sea)___ .
It is strategically located near the ___E:Sunda Strait U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunda_Strait)___ .
The northern part of Jakarta is plain land, some areas of which are below sea level,  and subject to frequent flooding.
The southern parts of the city are hilly.

It is one of only two Asian capital cities located in the southern hemisphere (along with ___E:East Timor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Timor)___ 's ___E:Dili U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dili)___ ).

Officially, the area of the Jakarta Special District is 661.23 km 2 (255 sq mi) of land area and 6,977 km 2 (2,694 sq mi) of sea area.  The ___E:Thousand Islands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thousand_Islands_(Indonesia))___ , which are administratively a part of Jakarta, are located in Jakarta Bay, north of the city.

Jakarta lies in a low and flat ___E:alluvial plain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvial_plain)___ , ranging from −2 to 91 m (−7 to 299 ft) with an average elevation of 8 m (26 ft) ___E:above sea level U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Above_mean_sea_level)___ with historically extensive swampy areas.
Some parts of the city have been constructed on reclaimed tidal flats that occur around the area.  Thirteen rivers flow through Jakarta.

They are ___E:Ciliwung River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliwung_River)___ , Kalibaru, ___E:Pesanggrahan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesanggrahan_River)___ , ___E:Cipinang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cipinang_River)___ , ___E:Angke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angke_River)___ , Maja, Mookervart, Krukut, Buaran, West Tarum, Cakung, Petukangan, ___E:Sunter River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunter_River)___ and ___E:Grogol River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grogol_River)___ .

They flow from the ___E:Puncak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puncak)___ highlands to the south of the city, then across the city northwards towards the Java Sea. The ___E:Ciliwung River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliwung_River)___ divides the city into the western and eastern districts.
These rivers, combined with the wet season rains and insufficient drainage due to clogging, make Jakarta prone to ___E:flooding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flooding_in_Jakarta)___ .
Moreover, Jakarta is sinking about 5 to 10 cm (2.0 to 3.9 in) each year, and up to 20 cm (7.9 in) in the northern coastal areas.

After a feasibility study, a ring ___E:dyke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levee)___ known as ___E:Giant Sea Wall Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant_Sea_Wall_Jakarta)___ is under construction around Jakarta Bay to help cope with the threat from the sea. The dyke will be equipped with a pumping system and retention areas to defend against seawater and function as a toll road. The project is expected to be completed by 2025.  In January 2014, the central government agreed to build two dams in Ciawi, Bogor and a 1.2 km (0.75 mi) tunnel from ___E:Ciliwung River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliwung_River)___ to ___E:Cisadane River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisadane_River)___ to ease flooding in the city.  Nowadays, a 1.2 km (0.75 mi), with capacity 60 m 3 (2,100 cu ft) per second, underground water tunnel between Ciliwung River and the East Flood Canal is being worked on to ease the Ciliwung River overflows.
In 2023, the ___E:New York Times U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times)___ reported that in some places Jakarta is sinking up to 12 inches (30 cm) annually.
Environmental advocates point out that subsidence is driven by the extraction of groundwater, much of it illegal.

Furthermore, the government's lack of strict regulation amplifies the issue as many recently built high-rise buildings, corporations, and factories around Jakarta opt for illegally extracting groundwater.

In fact, in a recent inspection of 80 buildings in Jalan Thamrin, a busy road lined with skyscrapers and shopping malls, 56 buildings had a groundwater pump, and 33 were pumping groundwater illegally.

This could be halted by stopping extraction (as the city of Tokyo has done), increasing efficiency, and finding other sources for water use. Moreover, increasing regulation through higher taxes or limiting groundwater pumping has proven to help cities like Shanghai, Tokyo, and San Jose relieve their subsidence issue.
The rivers of Jakarta are highly polluted and currently unsuitable for drinking water.
Jakarta faces significant ___E:air pollution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_pollution)___ , particularly during the dry season from August to December.
Dry air during this period allows pollutants to remain suspended in the atmosphere for extended periods, contributing to poor air quality.

Jakarta experiences a ___E:tropical monsoon climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_monsoon_climate)___ ( ___E:Köppen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification)___ : Am ) as classified by the system.

The city's ___E:wet season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_season)___ spans most of the year, from October to May. The ___E:dry season U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_season)___ lasts from June to September, with each of these months receiving less than 100 millimetres (3.9 in) of rainfall on average.

Situated in the western part of Java, Jakarta sees its highest rainfall in January and February, averaging 299.7 millimetres (11.8 in) per month, while the driest month is August, with an average rainfall of 43.2 millimetres (1.7 in).
Every year faces recurring issues, such as ___E:floods U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floods)___ and ___E:thunderstorms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorms)___ .
A ___E:cyclonic vortex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_tropospheric_cyclonic_vortex)___ leads to moisture convergence over a large area, including western Java Island.

Additionally, this vortex causes a mainly meridional monsoon flow, where near-surface winds blow almost perfectly from north to south over West Java. The impact of these predominant northerly winds hitting the rugged topography in southern West Java likely contributes to the increased convection that causes floods in Jakarta.
Average temperatures are very high with moderate rainfall.
During the day, the temperature usually hovers around 32 °C (89.6 °F) but drops to about 24 °C (75.2 °F) in the evening.
These are average temperatures, and some days can be hotter.

It's advisable to dress appropriately to handle the heat. January is the rainiest month, with over 300 millimetres (11.8 in) of precipitation, whereas August is the driest, with around 45 millimetres (1.8 in) of rainfall.
The average temperature in the coldest month (February) is 27 °C (80.6 °F), and in the warmest month (October), it is 28 °C (82.4 °F).
Sea temperatures range from 26.5 °C (79.7 °F) in August to 29.5 °C (85.1 °F) in March, April, November, and December.
Record low temperatures in Jakarta recorded 18.9 °C (66.0 °F), while the highest record reached 37.9 °C (100.2 °F).

Colonial architecture is apparent in houses and villas, churches, civic buildings, and offices, mostly concentrated in the ___E:Jakarta Old Town U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta_Old_Town)___ and ___E:Central Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Jakarta)___ .
Architects such as J.C.
Schultze and ___E:Eduard Cuypers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eduard_Cuypers)___ designed some of the significant buildings.

As the capital of Indonesia, Jakarta is a melting pot of cultures from all ethnic groups in the country.

Although ___E:Betawi people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betawi_people)___ are Jakarta's indigenous community, the city's culture represents many languages and ethnic groups, favouring differences in religion, tradition, and linguistics, rather than a single, dominant culture.

Jakarta is dominated by ___E:Javanese people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javanese_people)___ , followed by Betawi people, and ___E:Sundanese people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundanese_people)___ .

The ___E:Betawi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betawi_people)___ culture is distinct from those of the ___E:Sundanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundanese_people)___ or ___E:Javanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javanese_people)___ , forming a ___E:language island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_island)___ in the surrounding area. There is a significant Chinese influence in Betawi culture, reflected in the popularity of Chinese cakes and sweets, ___E:firecrackers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firecracker)___ , and Betawi wedding attire that demonstrates Chinese and Arab influences.
Some festivals such as the Jalan Jaksa Festival , Kemang Festival , Condet Festival , and Lebaran Betawi include efforts to preserve Betawi arts by inviting artists to display performances.

Mixed Sundanese–Betawi culture can also be found in ___E:Pondok Ranggon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pondok_Ranggon)___ , southeasternmost tip of Jakarta, namely Sedekah Bumi Keramat Ganceng Festival .

Traditional music is often found at high-class hotels, including ___E:Wayang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayang)___ and ___E:Gamelan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamelan)___ performances.

All varieties of ___E:Indonesian cuisine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_cuisine)___ have a presence in Jakarta.
The local cuisine is ___E:Betawi cuisine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betawi_cuisine)___ , which reflects various foreign culinary traditions.

Betawi cuisine is heavily influenced by ___E:Malay-Chinese Peranakan cuisine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peranakan_cuisine)___ , ___E:Sundanese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sundanese_cuisine)___ , and ___E:Javanese cuisine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javanese_cuisine)___ , which is also influenced by Indian, Arabic, and European cuisines.

One of the most popular local dishes of Betawi cuisine is Soto Betawi which is prepared from chunks of beef and ___E:offal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offal)___ in rich and spicy cow's milk or coconut milk broth.
Other popular Betawi dishes include soto kaki, nasi uduk ( mixed rice ), kerak telor (spicy omelette), nasi ulam, asinan, ketoprak, rujak and gado-gado Betawi (salad in peanut sauce).
Jakarta cuisine can be found in modest street-side warung food stalls and ___E:Hawkers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker_(trade))___ travelling vendors to high-end fine dining restaurants.
Live music venues and exclusive restaurants are abundant.
Many traditional foods from far-flung regions in Indonesia can be found in Jakarta.

For example, traditional ___E:Padang restaurants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padang_cuisine#Padang_restaurants)___ and low-budget Warteg ( Warung Tegal ) food stalls are ubiquitous in the capital.

The Jakarta provincial government relies on transfers from the central government for the bulk of its income.
Local (non-central government) sources of revenue are incomes from various taxes such as vehicle ownership and vehicle transfer fees, among others.
The ability of the regional government to respond to Jakarta's many problems is constrained by limited finances.
The provincial government consistently runs a surplus of between 15 and 20% of planned spending, primarily because of delays in procurement and other inefficiencies.
Regular under-spending is a matter of public comment.
In 2013, the budget was around Rp 50 trillion ($US5.2 billion), equivalent to around $US380 per citizen.
Spending priorities were on education, transport, flood control, environment, and social spending (such as health and housing).
Jakarta's regional budget (APBD) was Rp 77.1 trillion ($US5.92 billion), Rp 83.2 trillion ($US6.2 billion), and Rp 89 trillion ($US6.35 billion) for the year of 2017, 2018 and 2019 respectively.

Jakarta has many of the country's best-equipped private and public ___E:healthcare facilities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare_in_Indonesia)___ .

In 2012, the Governor of Jakarta ___E:Joko Widodo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joko_Widodo)___ introduced a ___E:universal health care U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_health_care)___ program, the 'Healthy Jakarta Card' ( Kartu Jakarta Sehat , KJS).

In January 2014, the Indonesian government launched a universal health care system called the Jaminan Kesehatan Nasional (JKN), which is run by ___E:BPJS Kesehatan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BPJS_Kesehatan)___ .

Two private companies, PALYJA and Aetra, provide piped water in the western and eastern half of Jakarta respectively under 25-year concession contracts signed in 1998. A public asset holding company called PAM Jaya owns the infrastructure.

Eighty per cent of the water distributed in Jakarta comes through the West Tarum Canal system from Jatiluhur reservoir on the ___E:Citarum River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citarum_River)___ , 70 km (43 mi) southeast of the city. The water supply was privatised by President Suharto in 1998 to the French company ___E:Suez Environnement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Environnement)___ and the British company ___E:Thames Water U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thames_Water)___ International.
Both companies subsequently sold their concessions to Indonesian companies.
Customer growth in the first seven years of the concessions had been lower than before, possibly because of substantial inflation-adjusted tariff increases during this period.
In 2005, tariffs were frozen, leading private water companies to cut down on investments.
According to PALYJA, the service coverage ratio increased substantially from 34% (1998) to 65% (2010) in the western half of the concession.
According to data by the Jakarta Water Supply Regulatory Body, access in the eastern half of the city served by PTJ increased from about 57% in 1998 to about 67% in 2004 but stagnated afterward.

However, other sources cite much lower access figures for piped water supply to houses, excluding access provided through public hydrants: one study estimated access as low as 25% in 2005,  while another estimated it to be as low as 18.5% in 2011.  Those without access to piped water get water mostly from wells that are often salty and unsanitary.

As of 2017, according to the ___E:Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Energy_and_Mineral_Resources_(Indonesia))___ , Jakarta had a crisis over clean water.
